composites.name: Nested Cellular Hierarchy — Live Cascade
composites.description: Fig 7 as a fully runnable temporal study: a cell's subsystems are a NESTED hierarchy of coupled processes running together. Transmembrane transport imports nutrients across the membrane; metabolism turns nutrients+enzymes into metabolites+energy in the cytoplasm; transcription reads DNA (six levels deep in nucleus.chromosome.chromatin.nucleosome.DNA) into RNA; translation reads RNA+metabolites on the ribosome pool into proteins; subunit assembly builds ribosomes from proteins (closing the loop); replication/repair maintains the DNA set point. Processes act on stores buried up to six levels down WITHOUT flattening the place graph. Runnable (default_n_steps + RAMEmitter); driver pools seeded by the environment, products start low and must be made — the nested cascade in motion.

composites.name: Biofilm Emergence — Live Topology
composites.description: Fig 10b as a genuine place-graph rewrite: biofilm emergence from free motile bacteria. The environment starts with a surface and free motile bacteria; running it makes them attach + aggregate into a nested microcolony, then mature by secreting ECM. Steppable topology for the loom run/animate feature.

composites.name: Interaction Modalities
composites.description: Fig 3a — four interaction-modality cards of the cellular interface: nutrient exchange (chemical flux), motile force (mechanical), growth rate, and electrical signaling. Each is a draft process: unit-bearing ports + a behavior contract, no update dynamics. Ports are wired to labeled stores so each quantity (and its unit) appears as a node.

composites.name: disintegration-spatial
composites.description: The disintegration study flagship: a single coherent CPM cell (CpmDisintegration, no metabolism/cobra path) sits centered on a shared 60x60 fields grid inside a radial acetate gradient -- the stressor species is `acetate`, the SAME molecule that is metabolic waste to the secretor and sole carbon food to the consumer in cell-cell-coupling-spatial; here its high peripheral concentration reads as a toxin. Low at the grid center (where the cell is seeded) and rising toward the periphery (peak 1.5, ring onset at radius 5, saturating at radius 18), the acetate field diffuses under spatio-flux DiffusionAdvection (D=4.0, no-flux/neumann boundary on all sides, so total acetate mass is conserved and simply relaxes toward its spatial mean). Each tick the cell reads mean acetate over its own CPM footprint (the CpmDisintegration `stressor_field` config points at the `acetate` species; the observable stays named mean_stressor); as the peripheral acetate diffuses inward the footprint-local mean rises and crosses viability_threshold=0.5 around tick 6-7, LATCHING the release flag. Once released, the process resorbs the cell toward zero target volume (resorb_per_tick=6.0) and sheds each tick's vacated footprint pixels as debris particles (up to 8/tick) into a shared map[particle] store, which a seeded BrownianMovement (SeededBrownianMovement, a reproducible drop-in for the stock spatio-flux process) then scatters deterministically. The cell fully dissolves (area -> 0) roughly 9-10 ticks after release, so a ~20-tick run shows hold -> cross -> resorb -> scatter end to end. Timing verified by direct Composite(...).run(N) inspection of state["obs"] during authoring (released_tick ~= 7, area == 0 by ~tick 16).

composites.name: A Store Hierarchy
composites.description: Fig 1b — A store hierarchy: the place graph of biological containment from tissue down to molecules, each store typed with its biological unit.

composites.name: whole-cell
composites.description: The composed whole cell — the paper figure mechanisms (thermal environment, uptake, a selectable Fig 5 metabolism [coarse | kinetic | FBA], a viability monitor, DNA-threshold division Fig 10-1, and disintegration) wired through shared cell/environment stores. It grows, divides once (mass conserved), then a thermal shock past tolerance collapses viability and converts biomass to debris. Swapping the metabolism mechanism gives three distinct life histories behind one interface.

composites.name: Cell–Environment Coupling
composites.description: Fig 4b — cell–environment coupling. The single cell is nested inside the environment (environment ⊃ cells ⊃ cell), and coupling processes wire across that boundary: environmental reaction–diffusion / production–degradation / mechanical stress act on the shared fields, while the cell senses those fields and writes back its uptake and traction — nesting and process coupling together.

composites.name: cellcell-crossfeed
composites.description: A tuned two-role cross-feeding pair (CpmColonyField) on a shared 60x60 grid demonstrating a metabolic handoff. A 'secretor' CPM cell runs the flagship microaerobic e_coli_core loop -- dynamic MM-limited glucose uptake (glucose_vmax 10.0) with O2 capped hard at 5.0 to force maximal mixed-acid acetate overflow -- and is fed by a LOCALIZED glucose depot (20.0 mM in the left columns 0-18, zero elsewhere) so glucose never reaches the consumer and the secretor plateaus once the depot is spent. A 'consumer' CPM cell has its glucose exchange fixed off (role-driven) and instead runs dynamic MM-limited ACETATE uptake (acetate_vmax 20.0) with O2 uncapped-ish (oxygen_vmax 20.0) to respire it. The two cells are seeded ~6 lattice cells apart (secretor x8-16, consumer x22-30) and acetate carries a high diffusion coefficient (15.0, vs glucose 0.4) so the secretor's plume crosses the open field and reaches the consumer's footprint before it starves. Over a 20-step run the consumer sits at ~zero local glucose, its local acetate rises as the plume arrives, and it net-grows on acetate alone (biomass 1.25 -> ~3.8). Regime tuned + asserted in task 4 (tests/test_cellcell_regimes.py).

composites.name: Orchestration — multi-timestepping through a shared store
composites.description: Fig 2a made runnable at the smallest honest scale: TWO processes updating at DIFFERENT rates through ONE shared pool store. FastProduction (interval 1.0) adds to pool.molecules every base tick; SlowConversion (interval 5.0) fires once per 5 ticks, converting a fraction of the accumulated pool into pool.biomass and drawing it back out. molecules ramps on the fast clock and saws down each slow firing while biomass advances in coarse staircase steps — two rates coordinated on one clock through a shared store. This is the dynamics behind Fig 2's multi-timestepping panel (a) only; panels (b) workflow-DAG and (c) event rewrites stay schematic. Runnable (default_n_steps + RAMEmitter).

composites.name: Nested Molecular Hierarchy
composites.description: Fig 7b — molecular compositions as a nested hierarchical composite. Molecular structure is organized as a nested place-graph across scales: an extracellular matrix, a membrane, and a cytoplasm containing a nucleus (chromosome → chromatin → nucleosome → DNA/histone), organelles (a ribosomal complex, mitochondria, secretory organelles), and cytoplasmic pools (proteins, RNA, enzymes, metabolites, nutrients). Six draft processes act on leaves deep inside this hierarchy — transmembrane transport across the membrane, replication/repair and transcription in the nucleus, metabolism and translation in the cytoplasm, and assembly of subunits into the ribosomal complex — so the topology reads like Fig 7b. All draft processes: unit-bearing ports + behavior contracts, no dynamics.

composites.name: protocell-autopoietic-v2
composites.description: v2 GENUINELY-LOCAL autopoiesis (peer-review M4 answer) -- the mechanism-level realization. Two fields on a 64x64 periodic grid, membrane phi (the exact Gaussian-annulus seed shared with protocell-autopoietic -- enclosed area 465px, mass ~630 at t=0) and interior precursor p (zeros at t=0). ProtocellV2 advances them with rd_step_v2, whose production term k_prod*phi*p*(1-phi/phi_max) depends on LOCAL precursor, NOT on any global binary_fill_holes closure observer (the observer appears only as a passive enclosed_area readout, never in the update). Closure-dependence EMERGES from geometry -- the membrane secretes precursor (s_p*phi) and is a barrier to it (mobility Mp*(1-alpha*phi) drops inside the membrane), so a closed ring confines the precursor it secretes into the enclosed pocket and sustains itself, while a punctured ring bleeds precursor through the gap and starves locally. Canonical params D=0.02, k_decay=0.01, k_prod=0.06, Mp=0.10, alpha=0.9, s_p=0.03, k_leak=0.03, k_cons=0.03, phi_max=1.2, thr=0.30, dt=1.0, steps_per_tick=50. Measured this build -- the closed loop sustains topological closure ~2451 internal steps (metastable, same order as v1, but with no global observer in the loop) while the precursor knockout (s_p=0) collapses at ~step 95; run and asserted within a ~1000-step margin comfortably inside the plateau.

Auto-generated from the fig11-evolution simulation (scripts/build_fig11_evolution_snapshots.py); one of three sequential frames of the running place-graph rewrite.

composites.name: Cell–Cell Coupling
composites.description: Paper §Cell–cell coupling (no dedicated figure). Two cell agents are wired to one shared environmental nutrient store: each senses the pool and depletes it, so their interfaces are coupled not only through shared state but through constraint — one cell's uptake reshapes the other's viability. Draft: typed ports + contract, no dynamics — node config carries only the timestep. cell_a_proc addresses local:CellAgent and cell_b_proc addresses local:RivalCellAgent: two draft roles with identical ports/contract (see interfaces.py), so an env can hand each cell a different handler/config (the compiler keys handler lookup by draft address, so two nodes sharing one draft address cannot receive different handler configs — see handler_envs.py). Competitive asymmetry (cell_a stronger than cell_b) and cross-feeding symmetry both live entirely in the env layer (law 4: swap the env, not this composite).

composites.name: overview-multiscale-composite
composites.description: Fig 1b — The multiscale draft composite: tissue ⊃ {fields, cell_population, cells ⊃ cell ⊃ molecules}. Molecular ODEs, FBA metabolism, structural packing, growth/division, and tissue-scale diffusion + ABM — all draft processes.

composites.name: cellular-interface-spatial
composites.description: The spatial translation of the cellular-interface study. The UNCHANGED CellularInterfaceHandler (local:CellularInterfaceHandler, the abstract fig03b cellular interface) is composed with a real 2D chemical field: a spatio-flux DiffusionAdvection process diffuses a left-low-to-right-high concentration gradient on a 40x40 grid, and a small field-point adapter (local:FieldPointCoupling) sits behind the handler's chemical port. Each tick the adapter samples the field's mean over the cell's footprint and feeds it to the handler as chemical_ext; the handler returns its net uptake flux (-uptake_rate*chemical_ext); the adapter deposits that uptake back into the footprint as a field delta, depleting the field where the cell feeds (niche construction), which diffusion then partially resupplies from the higher-concentration side. Same interface contract as the lumped fig04 composites, byte-identical ports -- only the process composed behind the chemical port has changed, now spatial. Only the chemical modality is spatialized here; mechanical, electrical and thermal remain lumped.

composites.name: cellcell-compete-div
composites.description: M7b dividing-population competition: two DIVIDING founder LINEAGES race for one glucose pool supplied at a fixed level from the boundary (Dirichlet BC value 8.0, chemostat-like), each cell growing by per-cell dFBA and DIVIDING at a volume threshold into a lineage (CpmCompeteDivision, a CpmGrowthDivision subclass), with a maintenance cost (0.10/tick) and a viability floor (biomass < 1.25 -> the cell is removed from the lattice via the native remove_cells -- a genuine death, not just displacement). Founder 1 is the FAST lineage (glucose_vmax 10, left) and founder 2 the SLOW lineage (glucose_vmax 4, right) -- the same 10-vs-4 uptake asymmetry as cellcell-compete, now heritable through division. MEASURED OUTCOME (M7b, tests/test_cellcell_m7.py): robust population-level COMPETITIVE DOMINANCE of the fast lineage -- by t=40 the fast lineage holds ~9x the slow lineage's biomass (seed 1: fast 122 in 48 cells vs slow 13 in 5 cells) across all seeds tested. This is competition-driven, not intrinsic non-viability: the slow lineage SURVIVES in monoculture under the identical supply/maintenance/floor (~22-33 cells; see the cellcell-compete-div-slowmono control) but is suppressed to a few cells when the fast lineage preempts the shared glucose (Tilman R*: the faster competitor draws glucose below the slow lineage's break-even). FULL competitive exclusion (slow lineage driven to zero) occurs at the deterministic headline seed by t~56 and in 2/5 seeds of a robustness sweep, but is NOT the robust outcome -- in the other seeds the suppressed slow lineage persists in spatial refugia near the supplied boundary. So the earned term is competitive DOMINANCE / suppression; strict exclusion is stochastic here, not deterministic.

composites.name: single-cell-in-a-field-chemotaxis
composites.description: CHEMOTAXIS variant of the flagship: the same single CPM cell (CpmCellField) in the same left-low-to-right-high glucose gradient on the shared 60x60 spatio-flux field, but now the cell ACTS on what it senses. chemotaxis_strength 50.0 turns on directed motion up the sensed glucose gradient -- each tick CpmCellField takes grad(glucose) of the shared field over the cell footprint and sets viva-cpm per-type external-potential force f = strength*grad(glucose), so the Metropolis pixel-copy is biased up-gradient (U(r) = -f.r). This closes the sense -> metabolize -> act loop the flagship deferred: the cell migrates up-gradient toward higher glucose (COM x ~18.5 -> ~39 over 20 ticks vs ~18.7 for the non-motile flagship), reaching a higher-nutrient region and acquiring/growing more than the stationary control on the same field. Identical to single-cell-in-a-field.composite.json except cell.config.chemotaxis_strength (0.0 -> 50.0).

composites.name: single-cell-in-a-field-mm
composites.description: Interface-substitutability twin of the flagship: BYTE-IDENTICAL cell<->field ports, but the internal metabolism behind CpmCellField is swapped from constraint-based dynamic-FBA (e_coli_core, O2-capped) to a lumped Michaelis-Menten / Monod metabolism (mechanism='mm', no cobra): uptake v = mm_vmax*glc/(mm_km+glc), biomass gain mm_yield*v, acetate overflow mm_overflow*v. The MM params are TUNED so the interface-level observables (biomass trajectory, acetate secretion, CPM growth, net glucose depletion) track the dFBA flagship -- demonstrating the paper's central claim (section 2 / Cellular interface) that different internal organizations can realize the SAME coarse-grained interface when they preserve the interaction variables relevant to that description. Same field, same DiffusionAdvection, same gradient as the flagship; only the box behind the ports differs.

composites.name: The Minimal Cell — Autopoietic Closure (runnable)
composites.description: Fig 8 as a fully runnable temporal study: the minimal cell's six coupled processes wired over FLAT scalar building-block pools (the form the ODE handlers actually integrate — membrane, lipids, metabolites, nutrients, amino_acids, nucleic_acids, enzymes, proteins, genes, energy as flat leaves). Containment assembles membrane from lipids; metabolism turns enzymes+nutrients into metabolites+energy; gene expression translates genes+amino_acids into proteins+enzymes; replication copies genes by spending energy and returns nucleic_acids; diffusion turns the metabolite pool over; mass-action reactions interconvert building blocks. Because the processes SHARE these pools, none stands alone — expression makes the enzymes metabolism needs, metabolism makes the energy replication spends, replication grows the gene template. This mutual production through shared components is autopoietic closure: run it and the catalytic/template pools (genes, energy, metabolites, nucleic_acids) hold a sustained steady balance while the cell's structural material (membrane, proteins, enzymes) accumulates — nothing collapses to zero, nothing explodes. This is the demonstration behind Fig 8b (the published draft nests these pools into container stores for display; the scalar-pool wiring here is what the handlers run). Runnable (default_n_steps + RAMEmitter).

composites.name: fig11-executable
composites.description: Executable compilation of fig11-evolution under handler environment 'fig11' — draft signatures replaced by conforming Process handlers (see compile.py). Runnable.

composites.name: protocell-autopoietic-v2-open
composites.description: v2-OPEN -- the EXTERNALLY-DRIVEN (open-system) variant of protocell-autopoietic-v2, the explicitly named remaining EMERGE step, built and MEASURED. Same two local fields on a 64x64 periodic grid (membrane phi -- the exact Gaussian-annulus seed shared with protocell-autopoietic-v2, enclosed area 465px at t=0 -- and interior precursor p, zeros at t=0) and the same genuinely-local update, PLUS a LOCAL open-system throughflow -- a uniform external precursor influx f_in, a first-order washout k_wash to an external reservoir (together a chemostat throughflow, exterior steady precursor f_in/k_wash), and an optional membrane turnover k_turn to an external sink -- so the system is no longer on a closed budget. Every added term is pointwise; NO global binary_fill_holes closure observer is in the update (the observer survives only as the passive enclosed_area readout, asserted structurally). f_in=k_wash=k_turn=0 reduces EXACTLY to ProtocellV2. Canonical open drive f_in=0.01, k_wash=0.02, k_turn=0 (plus the v2 params D=0.02, k_decay=0.01, k_prod=0.06, Mp=0.10, alpha=0.9, s_p=0.03, k_leak=0.03, k_cons=0.03, phi_max=1.2, thr=0.30, dt=1.0, steps_per_tick=50). MEASURED VERDICT (honest) -- external drive does NOT sustain closure indefinitely; it DESTABILISES the metastable v2 ring into faster runaway autocatalytic FILLING -- closure is lost at ~step 591 (~4x faster than the undriven ~2451), membrane mass runs away ~624 -> ~3092 (the whole domain fills), enclosed_area -> 0, and an ~80-point drive sweep found NO local drive reaching a bounded steady enclosed_area > 0. Controls stay load-bearing -- the s_p=0 precursor knockout still loses closure fast (~step 188) and a 60deg puncture is not healed (enclosed_area stays 0), so the drive never rescues closure. EMERGE therefore stays at genuinely-emergent-but-metastable closure; it is NOT upgraded to steady self-maintenance.

composites.name: Biofilm Development — Draft Interface

All three processes act on leaves inside a single `biofilm` store nested in the environment — the individual cellular interfaces become part of a collective (biofilm) interface that couples, as one composite, to the surrounding environment. All draft processes: unit-bearing ports + behavior contracts, no dynamics.

composites.name: The Cellular Interface — Made to Run
composites.description: Fig 3 as a fully runnable temporal study: a bounded cell (local:CellularInterfaceHandler) senses its environmental drivers and exposes typed interface ports. The environment supplies a chemical concentration (1.0) and holds a thermal driver ABOVE the cell's optimum (45 °C, opt 37 °C). Over the run the cell takes up chemical (Monod uptake → chemical flux), grows (growth_rate, accreting shape/volume), and its viability DECLINES by first-order Arrhenius thermal death because the temperature is above tolerance. This is the demonstration behind Fig 3b: the environment's drivers DRIVE the cell's interface ports. Runnable (default_n_steps + RAMEmitter): drivers → ports over time.

composites.name: cellcell-compete-div-slowmono
composites.description: M7b competition CONTROL (slow-lineage monoculture): the cellcell-compete-div slow lineage (glucose_vmax 4) ALONE under the byte-identical boundary glucose supply (Dirichlet 8.0), maintenance (0.10) and viability floor (1.25), no fast competitor present. MEASURED OUTCOME: the slow lineage is VIABLE on its own -- it grows, divides and persists (~22-33 cells by t=40). This is the necessity control that earns the competition claim in cellcell-compete-div: because the slow lineage thrives alone but is driven down to a handful of cells (and, at the headline seed, to extinction) when the fast lineage shares its glucose, the slow lineage's collapse there is caused by COMPETITION (resource preemption), not by intrinsic non-viability at this maintenance/floor. Without this control a slow-lineage collapse could not be attributed to competition at all.

composites.name: cellcell-compete
composites.description: Two competitor CPM cells (CpmColonyField) share one 60x60 glucose field and race for the same nutrient via independent per-cell dFBA. Both cells run the microaerobic e_coli_core role ('competitor'): dynamic MM-limited glucose uptake capped by their own glucose_vmax (10.0 for the left/fast competitor, 4.0 for the right/slow competitor), O2 capped to force mixed-acid acetate overflow, exactly like the flagship single-cell loop. Seeded left/right in non-overlapping half-open seed_blocks over a uniform ~3.0 mM glucose field so early dynamics aren't gradient-biased -- any asymmetry in growth traces back to the vmax difference, not seed position. Acetate is tracked as the shared byproduct field (diffuses away, not consumed by either competitor). Structural build target for task 3; regime tuning / competitive-exclusion assertions are task 4.

composites.name: The Cellular Interface
composites.description: Fig 3b — the minimal cellular interface. One cell (draft process) senses environmental drivers and exposes physical exchange ports (chemical, mechanical, electrical, thermal) plus higher-level cellular ports (growth rate, shape, signaling, objective, viability). Chemical and mechanical ports refine into subports (named in the contract). All ports carry biological units.

composites.name: cellcell-crossfeed-knockout
composites.description: Secretor-knockout necessity control for the cross-feeding regime: the cellcell-crossfeed composite with the glucose->acetate SECRETOR cell removed entirely, so no acetate is ever produced anywhere on the shared field. The only cell is the acetate consumer (its glucose exchange fixed off by role, acetate_vmax 20.0, O2 uncapped) seeded in the same place (cols 22-30) over the identical localized 20 mM glucose depot and diffusion constants (acetate 15.0 vs glucose 0.4). With no secretor plume to feed on and glucose it cannot eat, the consumer sits at zero local acetate and fails to grow -- biomass stays at its 1.25 seed the whole run (contrast the full cross-feed regime, where the secretor plume lifts the same consumer 1.25 -> 3.79). Closes the handoff-necessity argument: the consumer's growth in cellcell-crossfeed is genuinely caused by the secretor's acetate, not by anything intrinsic to the consumer or the field. Asserted in tests/test_cellcell_regimes.py::test_crossfeeding_knockout_consumer_fails_to_grow.

composites.name: single-cell-in-a-field
composites.description: The flagship spatial sense/act loop: a single CPM cell (CpmCellField) sits in a left-low-to-right-high glucose gradient on a shared 60x60 fields grid, diffusing under spatio-flux DiffusionAdvection. Each tick the cell reads local glucose over its footprint, runs one dFBA step (e_coli_core, O2-capped to force mixed-acid overflow), grows its CPM volume from the biomass it makes, and writes uptake (-glucose) / secretion (+acetate) back into the field as a spatial delta. Diffusion then redistributes both species: glucose flows in from the higher-concentration side to partially resupply the depleted halo around the cell, and the secreted acetate spreads outward into a plume. Tuned for GRADUAL, nutrient-limited, spatially-legible dynamics (a roomy grid, a real depletion halo, modest net consumption) rather than lattice-filling growth -- this is the run meant to become the flagship GIF (Fig 4 cell-environment coupling / niche construction, realized spatially).

A first-order transfer dA/dt=-k*A, dB/dt=+k*A drains the source into the sink while the total A+B is conserved. This is the dynamics behind Fig 1b's static signature: a process bigraph is an EXECUTABLE place-graph + processes — give a process an update rule and the wired stores evolve. Three functions — metabolism, containment, replication — each drawn at three grains, so that lumping a self-organized process (autocatalysis; membrane self-assembly; template replication) recovers its coarse closure. Read across, the three columns are autopoiesis: metabolism powers the boundary and the copying, containment concentrates both, replication reproduces the machinery they need. All draft processes: unit-bearing ports + behavior contracts, no update dynamics.

composites.name: development-evolution-spatial
composites.description: A growing CPM colony (CpmEvolution, study 8's dFBA growth/division reused unchanged) carrying a heritable per-cell glucose-uptake trait (vmax) that mutates on division (Gaussian, sigma=0.3) and IS under selection: higher-vmax cells divide faster on the shared depleting 60x60 glucose field, so the population mean vmax rises over the run. Emits mean_vmax/var_vmax (evolution) and rim_core_ratio (development: radial core-vs-rim glucose heterogeneity). The flagship of study 9's dual-control demonstration -- selection ON.

composites.name: molecular-equal-diffusion-control
composites.description: The molecular-interfaces study's causal control for molecular-turing-pattern: IDENTICAL Gray-Scott setup (same 128x128 grid, same static np.random.default_rng(1) seed_uv(n=128, seed=1) u/v seed, same F=0.037, k=0.06, dt=1.0, steps_per_tick=500) except Du=Dv=0.12 -- removing the differential-diffusion asymmetry (Dv<Du) that drives the Turing instability. With diffusion equalized, chemistry stays fully ON (the u*v**2 autocatalytic reaction term is unchanged) but the near-uniform seed never destabilizes: v_var stays ~0.0 (well below the pattern floor PATTERN_FLOOR=0.002) through the same 8000 total steps that pattern the Du=0.16/Dv=0.08 flagship -- verified directly in tests/test_gray_scott.py's equal-diffusion-control test (patterned==0.0, v_var<1e-4). Isolates diffusion asymmetry, not chemistry, as the causal driver of pattern formation.

composites.name: molecular-thermal-graded
composites.description: The molecular-interfaces study's thermal-channel demonstration: the same molecular-turing-pattern Gray-Scott setup (128x128 grid, static np.random.default_rng(1) seed_uv(n=128, seed=1) u/v seed, canonical Du=0.16, Dv=0.08, F=0.037, k=0.06, dt=1.0, steps_per_tick=500) PLUS a uniform raised `temperature` field (T=1.2, embedded as a static array since composite JSON state can't call an RNG/broadcast at build time) with Ea=0.15, Tref=1.0 -- GrayScott reads `temperature` from the fields store and scales the reaction term by the elementwise Arrhenius rate factor exp(-Ea*(1/T-1/Tref)); T>Tref speeds the reaction up. Retuned from an earlier Ea=1.0/T=1.5 setting (task-3 API-map finding): that combination OVERSHOOTS -- the raised reaction rate collapses the pattern to near-uniform (v_var~=0) by 8000 total steps, which reads as 'no pattern' rather than a graded one. Ea=0.15/T=1.2 instead legibly COARSENS the pattern relative to the no-temperature flagship at the same 8000-step count: v_var drops from ~0.0119 (flagship) to ~0.0096 (thermal) -- lower but comfortably nonzero (~4.8x PATTERN_FLOOR=0.002) -- while n_domains drops from ~12 (flagship, seed-sensitive 8-12) to 2, i.e. fewer, larger domains -- a real second-modality grading of the channel, not a chemistry collapse. Verified directly with gs_step at the same seed/params in tests/test_molecular_regime.py's test_thermal_channel_grades_the_pattern.

composites.name: Cell ↔ Environment — Live Coupling
composites.description: Fig 4 as a fully runnable temporal study: a real length-9 diffusing chemical grid seeded as a nutrient GRADIENT (low at index 0, high at index 8). The single cell sits at an interior index (4) and senses its LOCAL field through one typed interface — driving uptake (→mass growth), traction, and up-gradient chemotactic drift, writing uptake/traction back to the shared environment. This is the demonstration behind Fig 4b: the environment's fields DRIVE the cell's interface ports. Runnable (default_n_steps + RAMEmitter); the seeded gradient is what drives the cell (the source is off, so diffusion only relaxes it slowly).

composites.name: single-cell-in-a-field-steadystate
composites.description: M7d steady-state regime for the flagship single-cell-in-a-field — byte-for-byte identical to the flagship EXCEPT the CpmCellField adds three cell-independent steady-state terms so the pure-transient flagship becomes a chemostat-like regime with a genuine flux fixed point: a first-order glucose SOURCE (grid-wide relaxation toward a setpoint, glucose_source_rate 0.15 toward glucose_source_target 1.5), a first-order acetate DECAY sink (acetate_decay_rate 0.2), and a logistic biomass carrying capacity (biomass_capacity 0.5) that halts exponential growth at a stationary-phase ceiling. Run long (~120 ticks) it reaches a verified steady state — d(biomass)/dt and field fluxes fall below tolerance while the cell keeps metabolizing at maintenance. Field mass is deliberately NOT conserved here (open-system source/sink); that is the point of a steady state. Answers peer-review M7d, which noted every flagship claim is a transient with no source terms.

composites.name: Cell Division — Draft Interface
composites.description: Fig 9 (panel b) — division as a compositional rewrite. A prokaryotic cell replicates its chromosome (DNAReplication), segregates the copies toward the two poles (SegregateChromosome), and then splits — an event-driven graph rewrite (Divide) — partitioning state (DNA, biomass) into two daughters and incrementing the cell count. The daughters live as sibling stores under the shared environment, each re-coupling its own interface to it: division does not sever the coupling, it partitions the composition while the daughters remain coupled through the shared environment. All draft processes: unit-bearing ports + behavior contracts, no dynamics (division/segregation described as event rewrites in the contracts, not implemented).

composites.name: Grain Swap — Live Viability-Driven Switch
composites.description: Fig 5 as a fully runnable temporal study: a cell's viability is driven down by an external stress ramp (StressRamp); a GrainSelector swaps the active grain as viability crosses a threshold — while viable the COARSE grain grows the cell's biomass (linear yield), and once viability falls below the threshold the FINE grain takes over the dying regime, where biomass stops growing and DECAYS first-order. Exactly one grain runs per tick, so the coarse→fine switch — growth turning over to decline — plays out on-screen as viability slides. Low viability → fine grain.

composites.name: The Minimal Cell
composites.description: Fig 8b — the minimal cell: the three columns of Fig 8a wired into one composite. Constituents nest under their category stores — membrane ⊃ lipids, proteins ⊃ enzymes, metabolites ⊃ nutrients/amino acids/nucleic acids — so the part-of structure is explicit. Four processes — containment (lipids→membrane), metabolism (enzymes+nutrients→metabolites+energy+lipids), gene expression (genes+amino acids→proteins+enzymes), and replication (genes+energy→gene copies+nucleic acids) — are coupled through these shared pools, with generic diffusion (metabolites + proteins) and mass-action reactions keeping the building-block stores supplied. Metabolism powers replication and synthesizes the lipids that containment assembles into membrane, while expression supplies metabolism's enzymes: this mutual dependence through shared components is the minimal form of autopoietic closure. All draft processes: unit-bearing ports + behavior contracts, no update dynamics.

composites.name: fig03b-executable-alt
composites.description: Alternate executable compilation of fig03b-cellular-interface: the SAME typed cellular-interface contract realized by a SECOND, independent handler (CooperativeCellularInterfaceHandler) with a different internal mechanism — a saturable Michaelis-Menten membrane-carrier uptake, an independent cooperative (Moser/Hill, n>1) growth law, and Q10 thermal death — behind byte-identical cell ports, where the Monod twin uses first-order uptake, Monod growth, and Arrhenius death. Fitted so the interface observables track the fig03b-executable across the operating range chem in [0.2,2.5] to within ~10%. Runnable.

composites.name: cellcell-compete-mm
composites.description: Cell-cell (colony) interface-substitutability twin of cellcell-compete: BYTE-IDENTICAL CpmColonyField ports and the same 60x60 shared glucose field, but each cell's INTERNAL per-cell metabolism is swapped from constraint-based dynamic-FBA (e_coli_core, O2-capped) to a lumped Michaelis-Menten / Monod metabolism (mechanism='mm', no cobra). Each competitor keeps its OWN saturating glucose uptake v = glucose_vmax*glc/(glucose_km+glc) -- so the vmax 10-vs-4 asymmetry that drives competitive exclusion is preserved by construction -- then realizes growth by a fixed biomass yield (mm_yield*v) and acetate overflow (mm_overflow*v standing in for the dFBA O2-cap mixed-acid overflow). The mm_* params are TUNED so the colony interface-level observables (per-cell + total biomass, the competition ratio, total CPM volume, field glucose depletion + acetate plume) track the dFBA cellcell-compete within ~6%. This lifts the flagship single-cell dFBA<->MM substitutability up to the multi-cell colony composition level: same colony<->field interface, a different (cobra-free) box behind every cell.

composites.name: Cell Disintegration
composites.description: Fig 5b — cell disintegration as a grain-swap equivalence. A cell-level coarse-grained metabolism process and a molecular catalyzed-reaction network realize the same external interface at two different grains of description: coarse ⇄ fine. Lump the closed catalytic loops of the reaction network and you recover the coarse metabolism process; disintegrate the coarse process and you recover the network. Both grains are shown side by side, each wired to its own store cluster. All draft processes: unit-bearing ports + behavior contracts, no update dynamics.

composites.name: fig01c-place-graph
composites.description: Fig 1c — The place graph: hierarchical containment relations among stores, independent of process interactions. cell ⊃ {cyto ⊃ {rib, nuc ⊃ DNA}, mem ⊃ chnl}.

composites.name: single-cell-in-a-field-o2uncapped
composites.description: O2-UNCAPPED mechanism control for the flagship single-cell-in-a-field: byte-for-byte identical to that composite EXCEPT the CpmCellField oxygen bound is lifted (oxygen_vmax = 1000.0, so EX_o2_e is effectively unbounded instead of the flagship's microaerobic 2.5). With respiration no longer capacity-limited, unconstrained e_coli_core FBA takes pure aerobic respiration as the growth-optimal flux distribution and EX_ac_e sits at 0 for any glucose bound -- so the cell respires fully, grows faster, and secretes essentially NO acetate. Run head-to-head against the capped flagship this turns the study's acetate-overflow claim ("the O2 cap is what forces the optimizer into mixed-acid overflow") from an assertion about the code into a demonstrated experiment: capped -> acetate plume, uncapped -> ~0 acetate. Not a scientific result on its own; it is the flagship's foundational mechanism control (Fig 4 cell-environment coupling / niche construction, realized spatially).

composites.name: molecular-turing-pattern
composites.description: The molecular-interfaces study flagship: a Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion system on a 128x128 fields grid, seeded near-uniform (u~=1, v~=0 plus small Gaussian noise, plus 5 small nucleation patches of elevated v/depleted u -- the exact np.random.default_rng(1) draw from meta_modelers_guide/molecular/gray_scott.py's seed_uv(n=128, seed=1), verified patterning in tests/test_gray_scott.py, embedded here as static arrays since composite JSON state can't call an RNG at build time) undergoes chemical Turing pattern formation under the canonical differential-diffusion regime (GrayScott, pure numpy, no CPM/cobra/spatio_flux path at all). Each tick runs steps_per_tick=500 explicit Gray-Scott updates at the canonical spot regime Du=0.16, Dv=0.08, F=0.037, k=0.06, dt=1.0 (see meta_modelers_guide/molecular/gray_scott.py's module docstring/CFL note); v_var (the inhibitor field's spatial variance) rises from ~0 (near-flat seed) toward the patterned plateau as differential diffusion (Dv<Du) destabilizes the uniform state into emergent spots -- verified directly against the module's gs_step over the same seed/params: v_var reaches ~0.0117 by 8000 total steps (tick 16, patterned==1.0), matching tests/test_gray_scott.py's canonical-diffusion assertion.

composites.name: fig01b-store
composites.description: Fig 1b — A store: a typed container that holds a unit of shared state, accessible to processes. Here a single glucose pool typed `concentration`.

composites.name: protocell-vesicle-control
composites.description: The autopoiesis study negative control: IDENTICAL seed and process wiring to protocell-autopoietic (same static Gaussian-annulus phi seed, same Protocell process, same canonical D/k_decay/thr/dt/steps_per_tick) except production is knocked out via k_prod=0.0 -- collapsing rd_step's dynamics to plain decay+diffusion (see meta_modelers_guide/protocell/autopoiesis.py's rd_step docstring: 'k_prod=0 collapses this to plain decay+diffusion, the negative-control knockout'). Without self-production the membrane ring decays and its topological closure is lost well within the run window (observed < 150 internal steps in the Task-1 physics spike, well within this composite's first few ticks): enclosed_area -> 0 and persists -> 0.0, demonstrating that closure/persistence in the flagship composite is a genuine consequence of the autopoietic production loop, not an artifact of the seed geometry or diffusion alone. Protocell.__init__ explicitly restores any caller-passed 0-valued scalar config (k_prod included) that bigraph-schema's core.fill would otherwise silently refill from its non-zero _default -- so k_prod=0.0 here genuinely reaches the running process rather than reverting to the canonical 0.03.

composites.name: cell-sorting-spatial
composites.description: The sorting study flagship: a mixed 8x8 checkerboard of alternating-type 5x5-px CPM cells (64 cells total, 32 type-1 / 32 type-2, on a 70x70 lattice) demixes under differential-adhesion contact energetics alone (CpmSorting, the verified checkerboard config from tests/test_cpm_sorting.py) -- NO fields, NO metabolism/cobra path, this is the sorting *primitive* in isolation. Contact energies are tuned Steinberg-style: same-type contact is cheap (J(1,1)=J(2,2)=2.0), cross-type contact is expensive (J(1,2)=11.0), and contact with medium sits in between (J(0,1)=J(0,2)=8.0) -- so cells minimize free energy by clustering with their own type and pulling away from the other, at temperature=10.0 (Metropolis fluctuation scale). Each tick runs 10 Monte Carlo steps (mcs) of CPM copy attempts; hetero_frac (the fraction of intercell 4-neighbor lattice edges between two DIFFERENT live cells) collapses from its well-mixed checkerboard starting value toward a sorted low value while cell_pixels (the cohesion guard) and the per-type cell counts stay constant -- verified end-to-end in tests/test_cpm_sorting.py's Composite run.

composites.name: growth-division-spatial
composites.description: A single CPM cell (CpmGrowthDivision) grows via per-cell dFBA on an abundant, uniform 60x60 glucose field (spatio-flux DiffusionAdvection) and divides at a volume threshold using the native engine call divide_cells, compounding into a small lineage over the run. Tuned (glucose_vmax=1.5, vol_threshold=80, reset_target=40) for a clean 1->2->4->8->16 division staircase without runaway past the lattice.

composites.name: Evolution — Living Population
composites.description: Fig 11b — evolution by natural selection as a genuine place-graph rewrite you can play forward. A `population` (tree[node]) of identically-schema'd `cell` nodes — each with a heritable scalar `trait` and a derived `division_rate` — evolves under an `environment` whose `selection_optimum` gently DRIFTS over time (starting above zero). Each generation the optimum shifts, each cell's division rate is re-scored by trait↔optimum fit, and cells undergo BINARY FISSION: a dividing cell is REPLACED by two daughters, each inheriting its trait ± Gaussian mutation (the founder does not persist once it divides). The population grows to carrying capacity; beyond it the least-fit cells (furthest from the optimum) die. Over many generations the whole trait cloud tracks the drifting optimum — selection + mutation + division. Steppable topology for the loom run/animate feature.

optimum0.description: Starting favored trait value (the optimum at t=0).

drift.description: Shift of the selection optimum per generation (gentle moving target).

sel_strength.description: Selection sharpness — the Gaussian fitness width (fitness = e^{-s·Δ²}).

mut_sigma.description: Standard deviation of the heritable mutation step passed to each daughter.

div_rate.description: Per-generation division probability for a perfectly-fit cell.

composites.name: A Biological Process Bigraph
composites.description: Fig 1c — A biological process bigraph: processes are wired into the store hierarchy, each assigned a specific mechanism declared in its contract. Transcription reads the DNA template to make mRNA; translation reads mRNA at the ribosome to make protein; metabolism runs the enzyme-catalysed reaction network. The place graph (nesting) and the process coupling (wires) together are the bigraph.

composites.name: F₁Fₒ ATP Synthase — Live Four-Channel Transduction
composites.description: Fig 6 as a fully runnable temporal study: the F₁Fₒ ATP synthase as a molecular transducer that couples a proton-motive force across four TYPED physical channels. A ProtonMotiveRamp charges the substrate/proton drive (chemical_in) linearly over the run — the fig06 analogue of fig04's diffusing gradient — so the driving proton flux sweeps upward and MolecularMechanismHandler converts ONE coupled quantity into: ATP synthesis flux (chemical_out), a proton current across the PMF (electrical_out), a near-constant rotary torque on the Fₒ rotor (mechanical_out), and the non-conserved remainder as heat (thermal_out). All four derive from the single proton flux, so matter/charge/angular-momentum/energy are conserved: input PMF power (i_proton·pmf) = useful work + dissipated heat. This is the demonstration behind Fig 6b. Runnable (default_n_steps + RAMEmitter).

composites.name: A Molecular Mechanism
composites.description: Fig 6b/6c — a molecular mechanism as a process with typed physical channels. Fig 6b: the molecular interface exchanges matter (chemical, mol·s⁻¹), charge (electrical, C·s⁻¹/A), rotary work / torque (mechanical, N·m), and energy (thermal, J·s⁻¹/W), and is defined over molecular structure (PDB/SMILES) — no cell-level boundary. Fig 6c: the chemical channel refines into specialized subports — substrates, cofactors, catalysts, products. The mechanism is wired to a `ports` store (the typed channels + structure) and a `subports` store (the chemical refinement). draft process: unit-bearing ports + behavior contract, no update dynamics.

composites.description: Fig 1d — A process: typed input and output ports plus a configuration that maps inputs to outputs.

composites.name: development-evolution-no-mutation
composites.description: Identical to development-evolution-spatial except mutate=false (a BOOLEAN flag, not a mut_sigma=0.0 float override, which bigraph_schema silently drops): the heritable vmax trait cannot vary across divisions, so it stays exactly at the founder value with zero variance throughout the run -- the no-mutation control isolating raw mutational variance as the source of any trait shift (there is none to select on).

composites.name: development-evolution-no-selection
composites.description: Identical to development-evolution-spatial except selection=false: the vmax trait still mutates on division (raw variance builds up, var_vmax > 0) but every cell's dFBA glucose uptake uses the FIXED founder vmax0 regardless of its own trait, so the trait confers no fitness -- any drift in the population mean is undirected. The no-selection control isolating selection (not mutation alone) as the cause of the directional shift seen in development-evolution-spatial.

composites.name: condensate-cahn-hilliard
composites.description: The condensate study flagship: a scalar field phi on a 64x64 fields grid, seeded with near-critical noise (mean 0, uniform +/-0.025 -- the exact np.random.default_rng(0).uniform(-0.025, 0.025, size=(64,64)) draw verified stable/phase-separating in tests/test_cahn_hilliard.py, embedded here as a static array since composite JSON state can't call an RNG at build time), undergoes spinodal decomposition under Cahn-Hilliard dynamics alone (CahnHilliard, pure numpy, no CPM/cobra path at all -- an independent, uncoupled condensate-phase-separation analogue, not a mechanistic model of a specific biomolecular condensate). Each tick runs steps_per_tick=200 explicit CH updates at the pinned-stable M=1.0, kappa=0.5, dt=0.002 (see meta_modelers_guide/condensate/cahn_hilliard.py's stability note); phi_var rises from ~0.0002 (near-flat) toward the coexistence variance as phi separates into +1/-1 domains, while mean(phi) stays conserved near 0 -- verified directly against the module's ch_step over the same seed/params: phi_var reaches ~0.11 by 5000 total steps (tick 25) and ~0.38 by 10000 total steps (tick 50).

composites.name: protocell-autopoietic
composites.description: The autopoiesis study flagship: a scalar membrane-density field phi on a 64x64 fields grid, seeded with a deterministic Gaussian-annulus ring (the exact seed_annulus(n=64) draw from meta_modelers_guide/protocell/autopoiesis.py -- amplitude 1.0, radius n/4, sigma 2.5 -- embedded here as a static array since composite JSON state can't call the seed function at build time; enclosed area 465px, mass ~630 at t=0), undergoes autopoietic reaction-diffusion dynamics under Protocell (pure numpy, no CPM/cobra/spatio_flux path) with production GATED on the membrane still topologically enclosing an interior and self-limited by area relative to the seed's own enclosed area (homeostasis, not runaway growth). Canonical params D=0.02, k_decay=0.01, k_prod=0.03, thr=0.30, dt=1.0, steps_per_tick=50 (see meta_modelers_guide/protocell/autopoiesis.py's module docstring for the full derivation). Within the ~2000-step homeostatic-plateau window established by the Task-1 physics spike (metastable, not perpetual -- the ring eventually breaks down past ~2450-2650 steps even with production on), the closed loop self-maintains: enclosed_area stays > 0 and persists == 1.0 throughout.

composites.name: cellcell-crossfeed-realistic
composites.description: M7a realistic-diffusivity control for the cross-feeding regime. BYTE-IDENTICAL to cellcell-crossfeed (same localized 20 mM glucose depot in cols 0-18, same secretor/consumer roles and seeds x8-16/x22-30, same acetate_vmax 20 consumer, grow_per_biomass 30) EXCEPT the acetate diffusion coefficient is dropped from the flagship's 15.0 (a 37.5x legibility ratio) to 0.8 -- the PHYSICAL ~2:1 acetate/glucose aqueous ratio (glucose ~600, acetate ~1100 um^2/s). MEASURED OUTCOME (M7a, tests/test_cellcell_m7.py): at the physical ratio the handoff FAILS to complete within a legible horizon. The consumer's own footprint acetate peaks at ~0.21 (vs 1.60 at 37.5x) and its biomass rises only ~2% (1.25 -> ~1.28, vs 1.25 -> 3.79 at 37.5x) before it is competitively displaced off the lattice by the fast-growing secretor around t=20; extending the horizon does not rescue it. The secreted acetate does physically diffuse into the consumer's seed region, but at the physical diffusivity the plume is too slow and too steeply-graded to raise the consumer's own footprint concentration to a feeding level before displacement. Feeding scales monotonically with transport acceleration (consumer biomass gain +14%/+45%/+102%/+203% at 5x/10x/20x/37.5x), so the flagship cross-feed's accelerated transport is load-bearing for the legible handoff at this 6-cell-gap / 20-tick geometry, not cosmetic.
